title: Chroma Energy — cold outreach sequence & pilot runbook
content:
Goal: get intro call with Head of Digital Operations (likely Jane Ryu) and land 6-week pilot to prove cost/lateny delta vs their current hosted vendor.

Account snapshot (quick):
- Company: Chroma Energy (distributed grid management + DER orchestration).
- HQ: Austin. 1500 employees. Heavy EMEA ops.
- Tech signals: blog posts about on-device inference for edge meters, job postings for MLOps infra, uses Kafka + k8s, runs proprietary telemetry ingestion.
- Likely infra constraints: PCI-like security for grid control, prefers VPC or air-gapped option for command/control paths.

Primary decision-makers (tentative):
- Jane Ryu, Head of Digital Ops — risk/ops lead (target for intro).
- Marco Silva, Lead ML Engineer — technical champion (pilot design).
- Alana Briggs, Procurement — pricing/contract.

Top value props to surface (short):
- Predictable latency and throughput at fleet scale (shared-hosted -> dedicated pools).
- Unit-cost reduction via batching + prefix caching for repeated telemetry prompts.
- Private deployment option (VPC + on-prem packaging) addresses data residency and FIPS KMS integration.
- Rollouts & safe fallbacks to reduce risk during live control-plane usage.

Common objections & quick rebuttals (prep):
1) "We can't send control-plane data to cloud."
   - Rebuttal: offer Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) or on-prem appliance for the pilot. Outline data flow: telemetry stays in VPC, only model logits served inside private network.
2) "Latency jitter is unacceptable for command loops."
   - Rebuttal: propose co-located dedicated capacity in their preferred cloud region + SLO-backed latency targets; include stress test in pilot runbook.
3) "Switching models risks output regressions."
   - Rebuttal: show Optimize tooling for quality monitoring and prompt-eval regression alerts; include guardrails and canary rollouts.
4) "Pricing is opaque / too expensive."
   - Rebuttal: provide a 6-week pilot at fixed cost with clear per-token and per-embedding measurements and a simple cost comparison table vs current vendor.

Outbound sequence (email + call cadences) — draft templates (short & editable):
- Day 0 (cold email subject): "Reduce LLM inference cost for grid ops — 6-week pilot?"
  Body (short): "Hi {Jane}, noticed Chroma's work on distributed grid control. We help teams cut inference unit-costs and tighten latency SLOs while keeping models inside your VPC. Would you be open to a 20-min intro to explore a low-risk 6-week pilot? — Maya (Redwood)"

- Day 3 (follow-up): quick one-liner reference to a relevant case: "Quick note — we recently helped a smart-meter provider drop per-request cost 42% while moving to private VPC deployment. Quick chat?"

- Day 10 (value add): share short benchmark snippet: latency p50/p95 with specific model family, or a short explainer doc on on-prem inference packaging.

Call script (initial intro — 15 minutes):
- 0:00–1:30: quick intros + confirm roles
- 1:30–4:00: discovery — "what are your current inference bottlenecks? frequency, seq length, p95 latency targets, current provider/stack?"
- 4:00–8:00: talk constraints — data residency, audit logs, KMS needs
- 8:00–12:00: share top-line Redwood approach (hosted/dedicated/private choices) and a tangible pilot outline
- 12:00–15:00: next steps (pilot cadence, success metrics, signatures)

Pilot sketch (6 weeks) — measurable milestones:
- Week 0: scoping + NDA + network prep (VPC peering or on-prem installer access)
- Week 1–2: integration + baseline measurement (current vendor p50/p95, cost per inference)
- Week 3–4: Redwood run with dedicated pool or private deployment; run blue/green comparison for same prompts 
- Week 5: stress test (scale to projected peak) + security review
- Week 6: results deck, ops playbook, rollout recommendation + pricing proposal

Success metrics to propose:
- Latency p95 <= current p95 * 0.9 (10% improvement target)
- Cost per 1k tokens reduced by >= 25%
- No security incidents; pass customer SOC checklist (list to capture in scoping)

Data & access checklist for scoping call:
- Sample prompt set (10–50 prompts across control loop types)
- Expected QPS and peak concurrency windows
- Network topology: VPC in AWS/eu-west-1? Firewall/NAT constraints?
- Compliance checklist: SOC2, FIPS, cross-border data flow rules

Open questions / internal follow-ups:
- Confirm Jane Ryu email (current guess: jane.ryu@chromaenergy.com) — Liam to verify via LinkedIn + common connections.
- Need legal template for limited-scope pilot (PII-minimizing clause). Ask Legal: GTS-legal-pilot-template.
- Engineering: quick list of kernel/quantization options we can promise for on-prem installer (ask infra team).

Metric quick calc (back of napkin):
- Est. current: 100k requests/day * avg 150 tokens/request = 15M tokens/day. At $0.0008/token => $12k/day.
- Target: 25% reduction => save $3k/day => $90k/month. (High-level number to get procurement attention)

Next actions (this week):
- [ ] Liam: confirm Jane contact and org mapping (deadline: 2026-03-12)
- [ ] Sofia: draft pilot SOW skeleton + attach SOC checklist (deadline: 2026-03-15)
- [ ] Maya: send initial cold email + A/B test two subject lines (send by 2026-03-11)

Notes to self: keep email short, always drop an explicit low-effort next step (20-min intro). For Chroma, emphasize VPC/private option early to clear procurement roadblocks. Save longer technical detail for follow-up packet.

Rough content links to include in follow-ups:
- short benchmark PDF (attach after first call) — 'redwood-bench-grid-ops-v1.pdf'
- one-pager on Private deployment and KMS: confluence link above
- pilot SOW template: GH link in linked_artifacts

End of runbook (working).
